approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds from a population of real scored molecular graphs, retaining the best survivors and choosing parents from score quantiles. Its ordinary branch proposes a fragment addition or directed deletion with a graph neural editor. Only purchased edits that improve their original scored source train the editor by exact-action likelihood. A separate crossover branch remains active. A Gaussian process over raw count fingerprints selects purchases from the fresh graph pool, with the inherited mean screen after stalled progress. Canonical identity, duplicate, sulfur and size admission apply before purchase.
approach.novelty: Add admission-conditioned action sampling to the existing learned editor: remember the exact outcome of an attempted source/action and redistribute its probability only while that outcome is known to fail unchanged admission. This targets repeated known duplicate edits without changing the success learner. The supplied brief has no same-Parent siblings. Compared with the preceding editor introduction and earlier fixed motif supply, the new mechanism changes the feasible probability support using unscored action outcomes; it adds neither a vocabulary nor a learning objective.

observed_bottleneck: The actual code Parent n-cd97f70a82cb repeatedly spends its twelve-attempt ordinary opportunity on edits already known to fail admission. All fifteen Search sessions completed. Its exact-action learner remains confirmed: 354 positive paid actions, 10475 updates and full equal-session positive ordinary source gain 0.004970487405169856 versus 0.003968522922923545 in n-cf8d309c06de. This does not establish late or endpoint benefit: late paid gain is 0.0018123078245589424 versus 0.001982674692188382, and the complete endpoint mean is 0.5572964587203434 with paired delta -0.04973385749078766 and task_safe=false. The frozen policy audit identifies 105364 of 108281 duplicates after the identical source/action was already executed; late counts are 84458 of 85339 duplicates among 103027 attempts. The read-only complete-session audit in policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/plan/evidence-review.json rechecks these counts, chronology and all 4350 real feedback joins. It records equal-session late duplicate fraction 0.7683634442372724 and exhausted ordinary opportunity fraction 0.26174578169600426. This supports a known-support efficiency test, not a claim that an excluded alternative would score well or that the confirmed original learner failed.

adoptions.applicability: n-cd97f70a82cb completed all 15 sessions with measured exact-action learning: 354 positive real edits and 10475 updates, 1286 later paid probabilities changed. Its full ordinary gain prediction passed (0.004970487405169856 versus 0.003968522922923545), so mechanism_result=confirmed and falsifier=not_triggered remain. Late gain and ordinary incumbent gain declined; the complete endpoint delta was -0.04973385749078766 with task_safe=false. All 108281 duplicates remain in denominators. The new read-only exact-action audit identifies 105364 duplicate attempts after the same action had already been seen; this supports an admission-cache intervention without inferring which excluded alternative would score well. The complete Parent already implements the prepared1000-fragment vocabulary, exact source/action records, six-layer64-wide editor, session-local real replay and admission, with task walls42.2..285.2s below7200s, observed process RSS1416556KiB and CUDA allocation258695680bytes. It already materializes site-by-fragment probabilities; masking and sparse cached action/product links need no new model, package, oracle or corpus pass. hypothesis: Modify only the existing accepted-success editor proposal distribution by a session-local exact action-outcome cache. For canonical source s with verified ordered graph and fixed vocabulary, let q(add,i,f|s)=0.5*p_site(i|s)*p_fragment(f|s,i), and q(delete,k,d|s)=0.5*p_cut(k,d|s). The inherited static graph/size support remains unchanged; unsupported modes contain no complete supported actions. Before each attempted construction, K(a)=0 exactly for a previously established deterministic construction/identity/size/source-relative-sulfur rejection or a cached canonical product currently in real seen or current pool_seen; otherwise K(a)=1, including every untried physical action and every still-unknown alias. Sample q_K(a)=q(a)*K(a)/Z, Z=sum over all supported additions and directed deletions of q(a)*K(a), with jointly updated mode and site marginals. Product links persist across pools; pool-only duplicate exclusions expire when their products are absent from the next pool and real seen. Cache no unpurchased reward. Positive real actions continue to train the original unconditioned action likelihood. The causal prediction is that this dynamic support law reduces late duplicate attempts and exhausted opportunities, which may separately raise useful late paid source gain and the endpoint.

finding_summary.headline: Cache removes repeated-edit waste and raises late source gain, but final score declines
finding_summary.insights: Known-support waste was a real, removable obstacle, but removing it was insufficient for better endpoint search. The cache recovered admissible proposals while preserving uncertainty about unseen actions: all 3,273 remaining duplicate attempts came from previously untried actions, and 11,472 previously known but currently admissible actions were successfully reused. Temporary-pool exclusions therefore behaved as temporary membership constraints, rather than permanent novelty bans. This result supports the full conditioning law, including its construction-failure and pool/real-identity exclusions; it does not isolate which exclusion class contributed how much. The positive late source-gain result has a narrower meaning than progress toward the best molecule. Equal-session late ordinary source score fell from 0.522888 to 0.480871, and the corresponding purchased score fell from 0.461368 to 0.404960. Full-period ordinary positive gain also fell from 0.00497049 to 0.00418138, while ordinary incumbent-gain mass per session fell from 0.137427 to 0.114942. Larger improvements over weaker sampled sources can coexist with these declines; the changed sources and purchase mixture prevent a claim that the larger relative gain mediated an endpoint benefit. The Parent's earlier confirmed full-period learning result remains unchanged. The chemistry points to a remaining proposal limitation rather than universal scaffold collapse. Global typed scaffold counts were similar, 1,387 versus 1,426, yet two high-score strata narrowed from 27 to 13 and from 49 to 28 typed scaffolds. The number of accepted molecules with at least 50 heavy atoms rose from 246 to 413, while 171 tiny molecules with at most six heavy atoms remained. Reactive heteroatom junctions and unspecified stereocentres also persisted. These observations support a diagnosis of uneven access to useful connected cores and linkers despite efficient generation of new identities. A context-preserving core/linker replacement operator or a search scheme that explores such replacements could address that limitation; these data do not establish its benefit, a universal chemical filter, or the GP ranker as the cause. The retained MARS-inspired factorization and positive-action likelihood learner demonstrably operated. The cache is the registered adaptation to internal evidence; this host uses a fixed permitted-corpus vocabulary and GP-selected real feedback, not the paper's annealed chains, so no source-paper convergence or performance result transfers. The experiment settles this intervention's efficiency and late-gain predictions and its failed endpoint target. It leaves the broader learned-editor approach and separate retained-component contributions open.
finding_summary.results: All fifteen sessions completed. Joint conditioning was checked on 44,745 attempted actions: 338,376 legitimate known-action exclusions, 31,366 pool-only re-enabling transitions and no detected identity, normalization or feedback-join violations. The original raw-likelihood learner remained active, using 379 positive real edits and 10,350 updates. The primary efficiency test passed. Equal-session late duplicate-attempt fraction fell from 0.768363 to 0.052782; the underlying counts were 85,339/103,027 versus 1,138/21,159. Late exhausted-opportunity fraction fell from 0.261746 to 0.0000503, with 5,274/20,118 versus 1/19,946 exhausted opportunities. Duplicate fraction declined in every session; exhaustion declined in thirteen and stayed zero in two. No previously known exact action produced a duplicate in the Child. The separate late source-gain test also passed: positive gain per paid ordinary molecule rose from 0.00181231 to 0.00316586, with all 971 Child and 1,288 Parent late ordinary purchases retained; eleven sessions improved and four declined. Every one of the 435 batch purchase sets changed, and all 4,350 purchases joined accepted feedback, with 4,200 actual next-fit uses and 150 terminal censors. This did not improve final Top-1. Mean score was 0.547179 versus the code Parent's 0.557296, a paired change of -0.010118 rather than the required +0.002. Seed macro changes were -0.027158, -0.021113 and +0.017919. The paired task-safety rule found no material task regression against the code Parent; the separate formal-Anchor comparison was -0.059851 and failed task safety on sitagliptin. The mechanism is confirmed on efficiency and late source-relative gain; the endpoint target failed.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich amides, heteroaromatic diones and cyclic aryl amines, with unresolved stereochemistry, reactive junctions and large size tails
molecular.overall_character: This is an assessment of the accepted molecular output of n-a8f828a5ff9b. The frozen comparison marks both Child evaluation and pairing with actual code Parent n-cd97f70a82cb complete for Search seeds 0, 1 and 2. All listed Child and published Parent trajectories were read; no input path or task comparison is missing. Formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de is distinct and is not used as the code-Parent chemistry baseline. Each side supplies 4350 accepted optimizer molecules, with the fixed initial records excluded from population descriptors. These trajectories do not expose the chemistry of every internally generated, rejected or unpurchased candidate. The output contains ordinary indole carboxamides, N-rich fused diones, aryl ketones, sulfones/sulfonamides, pyrrolidines, piperidines, piperazines, azetidines and fused or bridged amines. Across the five tasks the digest ring-closure rates are 0.9368 to 0.9782 and aromatic-text rates 0.9299 to 0.9736. These are molecule-level SMILES-text flags, not ring counts or fractions of aromatic atoms. RDKit reads all 4350 accepted Child structures; median heavy-atom count is 30 and median perceived ring count is 4, but the size range is 1 to 120 heavy atoms. There are 171 structures with at most 6 heavy atoms and 413 with at least 50, versus 173 and 246 in the Parent. Conventional medicinal-chemistry families coexist with 542 N-halogen-containing structures, 27 O-halogen-containing structures, 177 divalent O-O matches and 34 acyl-halide matches. The corresponding Parent counts under exactly the same audit definitions are 516, 26, 71 and 4. These overlapping structural flags identify chemical liabilities, not measured instability, toxicity or synthesis failure. No Child molecule has an assigned atom stereocentre; 1696 have at least one unassigned centre, and only 13 have a formal charge. The Parent also has no assigned centres, with 1673 unassigned-centre structures and 14 charged structures. Diversity is moderate rather than collapsed: the complete Child panel has 1387 typed and 1127 generic Murcko scaffolds, but high-scoring molecules in each session cluster around a small number of families and many changes only alter substituents. Descriptor counts are read-only derivations, not additional objective scores. A high/low stratum below means the highest/lowest 29 accepted optimizer scores in each seed, combined across seeds; ties are ordered by evaluation. Chemical plausibility and missing-coverage statements are structural readings, without a synthesis route, conformational calculation, experimental property measurement, mechanism verdict or component attribution. Digest and comparison source: policy/requests/r0076-00-improve-L01-molecular-assess-57d67337db1bb351.json. Structural definitions, complete per-task audit index and aggregate counts: policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/summary.json. Byte-identical preservation of the legally supplied Child Search trajectories, plus published Parent source hashes: policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/provenance.json.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 accepted proposals are mainly compact, flat indole-carbonyl-phenyl assemblies: median 25 heavy atoms, range 1 to 36, with median 3 rings. Methyl, methoxy, hydroxymethyl and fluoroalkyl substitutions surround a carboxamide or hydrazide connection. The seed-1 leader is a 24-heavy-atom, 3-aromatic-ring N-cyano-N-phenyl indole carboxamide with methyl and hydroxymethyl substituents. Seed 0 instead ends with an aryl-nitroso N-methyl anilide leader; seed 2 has an N-N-linked, difluoromethyl hydrazide leader. These are chemically distinct polar junctions on a largely retained aromatic framework. Ordinary indole anilides are plausible synthetic targets, while the nitroso, N-cyano and halogenated-N variants need additional chemical scrutiny. Parent and Child both have median 25 heavy atoms; the Child has 130 nitrile matches versus 379 in the Parent. Evidence files (run-relative; each audit records both raw inputs and hashes): policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-0-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-0/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-cd97f70a82cb/seed-0/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-1-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-1/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-cd97f70a82cb/seed-1/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-2-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-2/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-cd97f70a82cb/seed-2/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl.
liabilities: The accepted set includes 139 N-halogen and 51 divalent O-O matches. Indole-N fluorination or iodination and peroxide linkages can be graph-valid without being ordinary stable analogues.
The aromatic nitroso group and N-N hydrazide junction in separate seed leaders raise reactivity and stability questions. Their recorded scores do not establish acceptable chemical behavior.
Small context-free species continue to consume accepted evaluations; the ring-rich leaders do not make those fragment-like outputs chemically useful.
missing_features: The favorable compact polar-carbonyl framework is not reproduced with comparable chemical quality across seeds: nitrile-bearing leaders coexist with nitroso and hydrazide alternatives. The gap is consistent access to compatible combinations, not global absence of a nitrile or an amide.

High-score core-connectivity coverage is limited to 8 typed and 7 generic scaffolds across the 87-molecule stratum. Broader compact ring/linker alternatives retaining useful carbonyl and polar placement remain undemonstrated; the observed scores do not identify one mandatory unobserved target scaffold.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy fluoroanilide scores 0.3051048083696145. The hydroxymethyl N-cyano anilide reaches 0.5188745216627708; nearby methoxy and unsubstituted-at-that-polar-position analogues score 0.50709255283711 and 0.4833240334107056. In the other seeds the nitroso-anilide and difluoromethyl hydrazide leaders score 0.471981152610369 and 0.42654444944303593. Water and hypochlorous-acid SMILES occur at zero. The high-score strata retain 3 rings and 23 to 27 heavy atoms throughout, with 29 nitrile matches, whereas the low-score strata have median 8 heavy atoms and only one nitrile match. This supports retention of compact aromatic-carbonyl context with carefully placed polar groups; it does not isolate a causal nitrile effect. The matched Parent also concentrates its high scores in 3-ring, 23-to-26-heavy-atom structures, including aryl-nitrile-containing indole derivatives.

per_task.generated_character: This set is larger and highly aromatic: median 41 heavy atoms and 5 rings, with a 120-heavy-atom, 16-aromatic-ring extreme. The seed-2 leader is a 40-heavy-atom, 5-ring fused N-heterocyclic dione joined through an arylamine/pyridine arrangement to a brominated aryl tert-butyl ketone. Seed 0 favors a more compact N-rich heteroaromatic assembly with an N-N linkage; seed 1 favors phenyl/pyridyl/tetrazole-containing structures bearing an aryl peroxide and a mixed anhydride. The leading seed-2 skeleton uses recognizable synthetic building blocks, although its crowded multiring substitution makes synthesis nontrivial. Other series include repeated-core and carbonate/anhydride-rich expansions. There are 211 structures with at least 50 heavy atoms, versus 191 in the Parent. Evidence files (run-relative; each audit records both raw inputs and hashes): policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-0-deco_hop.json; policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-0/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; nodes/n-cd97f70a82cb/seed-0/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-1-deco_hop.json; policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-1/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; nodes/n-cd97f70a82cb/seed-1/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-2-deco_hop.json; policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-2/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; nodes/n-cd97f70a82cb/seed-2/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl.
liabilities: The set contains 98 divalent O-O matches, 94 N-halogen matches and 4 acyl-halide matches. Mixed anhydrides, peroxide bonds and acyl bromides are especially questionable as stable end products.

Highly expanded, repeated multiring molecules reach 120 heavy atoms. Their synthetic effort and conformational/solubility consequences are not captured by the supplied structural validity or objective score.
The seed-1 leader has an unassigned stereocentre, and none of the proposed structures carries an assigned atom configuration.
missing_features: The output lacks consistent compact alternatives that retain the favorable heteroaryl/aryl connection without repeated-core growth. A larger ring count alone does not recover the leading arrangement.

Chemically conventional linker and terminal-group alternatives are uneven: one entire seed-specific high-score stratum retains peroxide chemistry. The score is insufficient to infer that peroxide, N-halogen or mixed-anhydride groups are necessary.

High-score scaffold coverage has narrowed relative to the Parent. Saturated ring replacements are scarcely represented in the full set and absent from the high stratum; their utility is unmeasured, rather than an established missing requirement of this objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial best is 0.548381482770623; the seed-2 arylamine/pyridine/dione leader reaches 0.6725083815909784, and the compact aza-rich seed-0 and peroxide-bearing seed-1 leaders reach 0.6210144165000526 and 0.6046712802768166. Tiny acetylene and water structures sit at 0.5. More size is not uniformly rewarded: the 120-heavy-atom, 16-aromatic-ring assembly scores only 0.5687285223367697. A conventional N-methyl dione analogue and N-bromo/N-chloro versions can all score 0.662670163606844. The gradient therefore distinguishes the arrangement of heteroaromatic and aryl substituents more than it certifies stability or rewards unlimited ring multiplication. The high-score strata occupy 13 typed/10 generic scaffolds, compared with 27/18 in the code Parent, and contain no fully saturated rings.

per_task.generated_character: The dominant successful chemistry is halogenated aryl groups combined with free saturated cyclic amines, including azetidines, pyrrolidines and fused or bridged amines. The full set has median 32 heavy atoms, 4 rings and 2 aromatic rings; 849 of 870 molecules contain halogens. The seed-1 leader is a compact 23-heavy-atom dichlorophenyl assembly with an azetidine and a fused bicyclic tertiary amine. Seed 2 combines a chlorinated diaryl sulfone/phenol region with a bridged amine and another small cyclic amine; sulfonate analogues are also present. Seed 0 retains a partially unsaturated N-ring, a pyridylaminomethyl group and pyrrolidine. These families resemble plausible medicinal chemistry, while their ring fusion and multiple stereogenic positions would require explicit synthetic stereocontrol. Evidence files (run-relative; each audit records both raw inputs and hashes): policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-0-drd2_docking.json; policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-0/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl; nodes/n-cd97f70a82cb/seed-0/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-1-drd2_docking.json; policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-1/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl; nodes/n-cd97f70a82cb/seed-1/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-2-drd2_docking.json; policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-2/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl; nodes/n-cd97f70a82cb/seed-2/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl.
liabilities: Dense cyclic-amine combinations and aryl halogenation may complicate physicochemical behavior; no solubility, selectivity, toxicity or experimental affinity measurement is available.

The full accepted set reaches 120 heavy atoms and includes 21 acyl-halide matches, versus 2 in the Parent. These liabilities are outside the compact high-score family rather than necessary ingredients of its chemistry.
Neutral SMILES with unresolved ring stereochemistry leave concrete molecular identity incomplete for prospective synthesis or three-dimensional interpretation.
missing_features: Basic cyclic amine chemistry is already abundant; the gap is consistent placement in compact aryl/amine assemblies without oversized scaffold recombination. The 186 molecules with at least 50 heavy atoms, versus 42 in the Parent, are absent from the high-score stratum.

Every high-stratum molecule has at least one unassigned atom stereocentre and none has an assigned configuration. Explicit stereoisomer coverage for the fused/bridged and substituted amines is missing.

Only one accepted molecule has a formal charge. Chemically plausible ionisation-state alternatives are scarcely represented even though amines are common; the supplied scores do not test whether charge-state enumeration would help.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact dichlorophenyl/azetidine/bicyclic-amine leader scores 0.9932455905087465. A diaryl-sulfone/bridged-amine example reaches 0.9863412374663348. In contrast, a dichlorophenyl sulfonamide whose pyrrolidine nitrogen is sulfonylated scores 0.0001542080382381353: aryl halogens and a ring nitrogen alone do not reproduce the favorable free-amine arrangement. All 87 high-stratum molecules contain a nonamide neutral saturated-ring nitrogen and a saturated ring, with 22 to 34 heavy atoms; the low strata include both very small fragments and bulky amide/sulfonyl-rich assemblies. The Child high strata have 49 sulfonyl matches versus none in the Parent high strata and median size 29 versus 27 heavy atoms. These are different sampled chemical families, not proof that sulfonyl addition caused the score differences or a claim about a binding pose.

per_task.generated_character: The accepted structures are generally medium-to-large heteroaromatic/lactam assemblies, with median 38 heavy atoms and 5 rings, versus 32 and 4 in the Parent. Seed 0 combines a fused N-rich dione with a biaryl group and an alkyl-substituted N-sulfonyl piperidine. That piperidine nitrogen is sulfonamide-bound, so its presence is not evidence for a free basic amine. Seed 1 uses a fused dione/indole assembly joined through a carbon attached to ring nitrogens and a substituted piperidine. Seed 2 reaches aryl diones with an ethoxy-linked N-methylpiperazine. Amide, sulfonamide, biaryl and aminoether motifs are recognizable synthetic chemistry, but selected N,N- or N,O-linked junctions are less routine. The full range is 1 to 73 heavy atoms. liabilities: The output can make a ring nitrogen nonbasic by sulfonylating it; a ring count or nitrogen count therefore overstates useful functional-group diversity.

Some late products connect an aryl oxygen and piperazine through an O-CH2-N junction, while others use N-O or N-N junctions. Those are distinct chemical stability questions, not interchangeable versions of a conventional ethoxy linker.
Unassigned stereocentres occur in 284 accepted structures, with no assigned configurations. Larger biaryl assemblies also carry unmeasured conformational and physicochemical costs.
missing_features: The available ring, amide and amine groups do not yield broad high-score combinations of core connectivity and linker geometry: the high-score scaffold set is smaller than the Parent set, despite larger typical molecules.
More compact alternatives preserving the favorable biaryl/polar-core relationship are unevenly covered; replacing a complete assembly with a small polar fragment loses the observed score.

The seed-1 aminal-like connections and late N,O-linked aminoether variants lack demonstrated configurational and chemical stability. The trajectories establish neither one required target pharmacophore nor the value of any unobserved replacement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best initial structure scores 0.1678386594791329. In the seed-0 biaryl/sulfonamide/dione family, methyl-, ethyl- and propyl-substituted piperidine examples score 0.23174488732966075, 0.23393135998842673 and 0.23480114051887288. The other seed leaders, containing an indole/piperidine connection or an aryl aminoether/piperazine, score 0.21332278949264138 and 0.21665575155108543. Isolated guanidine, ammonia and water occur at zero. The evidence favors retention and modest tuning of a connected aromatic/polar/ring assembly rather than simply introducing a nitrogen atom. High strata span 25 to 45 heavy atoms and 4 to 6 rings. They contain 28 typed/19 generic scaffolds versus 49/37 in the Parent; their median heavy-atom count is 37 versus 31. Small homologation gains within one family do not establish a general reward for growth.

per_task.generated_character: This output concentrates on compact N-rich fused dione or iminone systems, often joined to a phenol and decorated with fluoroalkyl or fluoromethoxy groups. Median size is 27 heavy atoms with 4 rings, matching the Parent medians; the range is 1 to 43 heavy atoms. The seed-2 leader has 24 heavy atoms, 3 aromatic rings, a phenol, an exocyclic imine, a carbonyl, a branched fluoroalkyl group and an N-F bond. Seed 0 retains a fluorinated unsaturated oxygen ring, while seed 1 produces a more extensively fused aromatic system with an allyl group, imine and fluoromethoxy substituent. Carbon-fluorinated heterocycle chemistry is accessible, but N-fluorinated imide-like products and unresolved fluoroalkyl stereochemistry make the set chemically questionable. Evidence files (run-relative; each audit records both raw inputs and hashes): policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-0-sitagliptin_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-0/trajectories/sitagliptin_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-cd97f70a82cb/seed-0/trajectories/sitagliptin_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-1-sitagliptin_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-1/trajectories/sitagliptin_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-cd97f70a82cb/seed-1/trajectories/sitagliptin_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-2-sitagliptin_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-2/trajectories/sitagliptin_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-cd97f70a82cb/seed-2/trajectories/sitagliptin_mpo.jsonl.
liabilities: There are 250 N-halogen-containing molecules versus 174 in the Parent, including the overall leader. These bonds and exocyclic imines raise stability/reactivity questions that the objective values do not answer.
The set includes 60 structures with at most 6 heavy atoms, versus 48 in the Parent, despite the high-score stratum requiring a retained multiring context.
Late heavily fluorinated ether substitutions can lower scores while retaining the core; the output does not show that more halogenation or branching is a chemically or numerically reliable direction.
missing_features: Chemically conventional alternatives combining compact fluorinated side chains with suitable carbonyl/imine placement are not reliably sustained across seeds. The issue is the arrangement and bond environment of the polar groups, not an inability to add fluorine.
Fluoroalkyl and fluorinated-ring stereochemistry remains unspecified: 247 structures have an unassigned centre and none has an assigned configuration.

High-score output is restricted to 14 typed/9 generic scaffolds. Saturated-ring and free cyclic-amine combinations are sparsely sampled here, although the generator can produce them elsewhere; their benefit for this objective has not been observed and is not asserted.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: In the same seed-2 phenol/iminone family, the branched CH(CH3)CH2F example scores 0.5167064329714901, the CH(F)CH3 example 0.4576218003401054 and the isopropyl example 0.40280679508865025. A more heavily branched ether/fluoroalkyl extension falls to 0.006839250937567302. Fluorine alone scores 1.1043196211273875e-26. The observed gradient favors a compact, specific combination of polar core and fluorinated side chain over either a free halogen or unrestricted decoration; it does not prove that the N-F bond is beneficial. The 87 high-stratum molecules have 22 to 29 heavy atoms and include 63 N-halogen matches versus 33 in the Parent. The Parent seed-0 leader reaches 0.48161648023481884 with a carbon-fluorinated N-ring and N-methyl dione chemistry rather than N-halogenation, providing an observed conventional alternative family without isolating which change matters.

A 120-heavy-atom, 16-aromatic-ring assembly scores 0.5687285223367697 in its own session, while a 40-heavy-atom, 5-ring structure in that objective reaches 0.6725083815909784. Another high-score family spans only 22 to 34 heavy atoms while its full accepted population includes 186 molecules of at least 50. These are within-objective associations across observed molecules, not a universal optimum size or a causal effect of the Child intervention. transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve useful molecular context while controlling both fragmentation and repeated-core growth.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide connected replacement, linker and ring changes that retain several useful groups together while allowing coherent growth or contraction. Learn which sizes and contexts matter from current-session accepted observations. Do not turn these descriptive ranges into a fixed universal size cutoff or claim that eliminating the tails has already improved endpoints.

transferable_gaps.evidence: For n-a8f828a5ff9b on the complete accepted Search panel, N-halogen, O-halogen, divalent O-O and acyl-halide matches occur in 542, 27, 177 and 34 molecules; matched Parent n-cd97f70a82cb has 516, 26, 71 and 4 under the identical audit patterns. Counts overlap. N-methyl, N-bromo and N-chloro versions in one aromatic dione family all have the observed score 0.662670163606844, and a separate high-score family frequently retains N-F chemistry. Thus neither successful parsing nor favorable objective value establishes stable product chemistry. These counts use the recorded SMARTS, including [O;X2]-[O;X2] for the O-O flag, and do not overwrite broader historical alert definitions. Sources and definitions: policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/summary.json and its indexed per-session audits; raw-input provenance: policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/provenance.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: Valence-valid assembly does not reliably distinguish conventional end-product bonds from reactive heteroatom junctions.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent bond environments during construction so ordinary aryl/alkyl halogenation, amides and ethers can be varied separately from N-halogen, O-halogen, peroxide, mixed-anhydride and acyl-halide chemistry. Supply chemically coherent alternatives through the same task-blind search. These alerts justify a chemical capability gap, not a validated blanket filter, a new reward, or evidence that the cache caused the liabilities.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Among 4350 accepted structures from source n-a8f828a5ff9b, none has an assigned atom stereocentre, 1696 have an unassigned centre and only 13 have a formal charge. The matched code Parent n-cd97f70a82cb has the same absence of assignment, 1673 structures with unassigned centres and 14 charged structures. Every molecule in one 87-member high-score stratum has unresolved atom stereochemistry while containing a saturated ring nitrogen. Thus this is a persisting representational gap, not a newly demonstrated loss of stereochemical capability. The measurements concern atom configurations and formal-charge encodings, not an assay of solution protonation or binding stereoselectivity. Sources: policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/summary.json and policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/provenance.json, with indexed raw trajectories and audits.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not specify stereogenic molecular identities, and ionisation-state coverage remains sparse in amine-rich chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve existing configurations and make newly created stereocentres explicit, with chemically plausible stereoisomer and ionisation-state alternatives treated as identifiable de novo choices under canonical/isomeric identity. Use only current-session accepted feedback to test their usefulness. No score benefit, protonation preference or three-dimensional pose follows from the present absence of those alternatives.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-a8f828a5ff9b clearly reaches nitriles, carbonyl-linked aromatics, sulfonyl groups and several saturated amine-ring types; none is globally absent. Across all accepted Search molecules there are 1387 typed/1127 generic scaffolds versus 1426/1014 for actual code Parent n-cd97f70a82cb, so a claim of global scaffold collapse would be wrong. Nevertheless, separate 87-molecule high-score strata contain only 13 typed/10 generic scaffolds versus Parent 27/18, and 28/19 versus 49/37. Another stratum has 33/30 versus 19/16, showing that the restriction is uneven rather than universal. The source and comparator share initial records and Search seeds; this is chemistry association, not independent replication or component contribution. Definitions and session-level conditions remain in policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/summary.json and the trajectory mapping in policy/scratch/r0076-00-improve-L01/molecular/provenance.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: Available functional groups do not translate into consistently broad high-score combinations of core connectivity, saturation and linker chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable coherent core, ring-saturation and linker replacements while retaining compatible aromatic and polar groups, rather than relying mainly on terminal decorations within a favored scaffold. Distinguish free amines from amide/sulfonamide-bound nitrogens and carbon-bound fluorine from heteroatom-bound fluorine. Let each clean session discover which combinations help; no benchmark identity, prescribed target scaffold or uniform diversification requirement is supported.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
